newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russia's Primakov in Strasbourg for Europe talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov in Strasbourg for Europe talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived in Strasbourg on Monday for talks with European Union ministers and the Council of Europe.

Primakov, Moscow's chief negotiator in tough talks on NATO's plans to expand into formerly Communist central and eastern Europe, was to meet the so-called troika of past, present and future holders of the European Union's rotating presidency.

Diplomats said the talks with Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, Luxembroug Foreign Minister Jacques Poos and Irish European Affairs Minister Gay Mitchell would cover EU-Russia cooperation and consolidating peace in the Balkans as well as what is known as the new European security architecture.

Primakov is to meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana in Luxembourg on Tuesday for a new round of talks on a Russia-NATO agreement meant to ease Moscow's opposition to the admission of some of its former satellites to the Atlantic alliance.

Russia continues to oppose the Western alliance's plans to invite former Warsaw Pact states -- probably Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic initially -- to become members and has sought help from European NATO states in pressing its concerns with the United States.
The talks are stuck over Moscow's insistence that NATO pledge formally not to deploy nuclear or conventional forces on the soil of new member states or build military infrastructure there.
Russia was admitted to the 40-nation Council of Europe last year despite controversy over its civil rights record and repression in breakaway Chechnya, where it has since reached a peace agreement.
President Boris Yeltsin caused surprise but no enthusiasm in March when he said Russia wanted to join the EU, a move no one in Brussels or member states think is realistic in the forseeable future.
